Tawḥīd for Children — Complete Lesson Slides
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 1
Opening
Al-Madrasatu An-Nuriyyah · Islamic Studies Unit
تَعْلِيمُ الصِّبْيَانِ التَّوْحِيدَ
Teaching Children Tawḥīd
By Shaykh al-Islām al-Imām al-Mujaddid
Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Tamīmī al-Najdī رحمه الله
d. 1206 AH
Islamic Studies · Ages 8–14 · Levels 2 & 3
Youth Educated… Family Cultivated… World Illuminated amanschoolmn.org

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 1: Cover

  • Open the class with Basmalah and a duʿāʾ together — set the spiritual atmosphere.
  • Introduce the author: Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, his title (al-Mujaddid), and why he wrote this book.
  • Build excitement: "By the end of this unit you will be able to answer the three most important questions in the universe."
  • Establish the Q&A format of the book — students will be asked, they will answer.
Before showing slide — open with dhikr
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ · بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى سَيِّدِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ، وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَأَصْحَابِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ، أَمَّا بَعْدُ.

[Turn to class] We begin with the same words that our book begins with. This is how the scholars always open their works — praising Allāh, sending peace on the Prophet ﷺ, and then beginning.
Introduce the book
Today we begin studying one of the most important books ever written for Muslim children. Its title is: تَعْلِيمُ الصِّبْيَانِ التَّوْحِيدَ — Teaching Children Tawḥīd. The word Ṣibyān — صِبْيَان — means children. That's you. This book was written specifically FOR you, so you can know the most important thing in all of Islām.
About the author
The author is Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Tamīmī al-Najdī. The scholars gave him the title al-Mujaddid — الْمُجَدِّد — the Reviver. Because at his time — about 300 years ago in Arabia — many Muslims had forgotten the basics of Tawḥīd and were mixing their religion with Shirk. He spent his life reviving what the Prophet ﷺ taught. He passed away in 1206 AH. This short book is one of his most beloved works.
Create excitement
Here's a promise: by the end of this unit, you will be able to answer three questions — the same three questions the angels will ask you in the grave. Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet? Let's begin. بسم الله.
⏱ Pacing Guide

Session 1 of 7

Week 1 — Unit launch. ~15 min. No prior knowledge needed.

📋 7-week unit total: 1 session/week × ~60 min = ~7 hours. This slide = ~15 min.

⚠ Do NOT rush. It is better to finish 5 slides deeply than 10 slides superficially.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• Open every Tawḥīd class with the same duʿāʾ — makes it a ritual students look forward to.

• Write the book's Arabic title on the board large and have students copy and read it.

• Ask: "Has anyone heard of this book before? Does anyone know what Tawḥīd means?" — gauge prior knowledge warmly.

• The opening of the original text (pages 7–8) begins exactly with أعوذ بالله, بسم الله, الحمد لله — model reading it together to connect students to the classical text.

• If you have a physical copy of the book — show it. Connecting students to a real Arabic text is powerful.

Al-Madrasatu An-Nuriyyah (AMAN)
Opening of the Text — Page 7–8
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 2
Opening
The Book's Openingأَمَّا بَعْدُ
The Classical Opening — Memorize Together أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى سَيِّدِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَأَصْحَابِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ · أَمَّا بَعْدُ
Word by Word Breakdown
ArabicTranslation
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِAll praise belongs to Allāh
رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَLord of all the worlds
وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُAnd blessings and peace
عَلَى سَيِّدِ الْمُرْسَلِينَUpon the leader of the Messengers
وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَأَصْحَابِهِAnd upon his family and companions
أَجْمَعِينَAll of them
أَمَّا بَعْدُAs for what follows / To proceed
The Purpose Statement — Page 8
Core Sentence of the Book فَهَذِهِ رِسَالَةٌ نَافِعَةٌ فِيمَا يَجِبُ عَلَى الإِنْسَانِ أَنْ يُعَلِّمَ الصِّبْيَانَ "This is a beneficial treatise — regarding what is something every person must do — to teach the children"
📖 أَمَّا بَعْدُ is a classical Arabic phrase meaning "To proceed" or "As for what follows" — used by scholars to transition from the opening praise into the actual content of their book. The Prophet ﷺ himself used this phrase in his speeches!

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 2: The Book's Opening — Al-Basmalah & Purpose

  • Read and understand every phrase of the classical opening from the text.
  • Memorize the Basmalah, Taʿawwudh, Ḥamdallah and Ṣalawāt opening.
  • Know the meaning of أَمَّا بَعْدُ and why it is used.
  • Know the purpose statement: فَهَذِهِ رِسَالَةٌ نَافِعَةٌ فِيمَا يَجِبُ عَلَى الإِنْسَانِ أَنْ يُعَلِّمَ الصِّبْيَانَ.
Read together
Let's read the opening of this book together — exactly as the author wrote it. First: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ — we seek refuge in Allāh from the accursed Shayṭān. Then: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ — in the name of Allāh, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. [Lead students in reading each line].
The Ḥamdallah
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ — All praise belongs to Allāh, Lord of ALL the worlds. The author doesn't start with 'I' or 'my book' — he starts with ALLĀH. This is the adab — the etiquette — of Islamic scholarship. Always begin by praising Allāh.
The Ṣalawāt
وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى سَيِّدِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ — blessings and peace upon the LEADER of the Messengers. سَيِّد means master, chief, leader. Our Prophet ﷺ is the leader of ALL the Messengers. وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَأَصْحَابِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ — and upon his family and companions, ALL of them.
أَمَّا بَعْدُ
Then: أَمَّا بَعْدُ — 'As for what follows.' This is a classical Arabic transition phrase — the Prophet ﷺ used it in his sermons. It signals: the praise is done, now here comes the actual content. Then the author says: فَهَذِهِ رِسَالَةٌ نَافِعَةٌ — 'This is a BENEFICIAL treatise.' He's not being modest — he's stating its purpose. It is BENEFICIAL because its content is Tawḥīd, and nothing is more beneficial.

Session 1 of 7

Week 1 — Same session as slide 1. ~20 min.

📋 7-week unit total: 1 session/week × ~60 min = ~7 hours. This slide = ~20 min.

⚠ Do NOT rush. It is better to finish 5 slides deeply than 10 slides superficially.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• The classical opening (Taʿawwudh → Basmalah → Ḥamdallah → Ṣalawāt → Ammā baʿd) is a COMPLETE Islamic format that every student should learn. Consider having them memorize this full opening.

• سَيِّدُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ is a strong title — contrast with the humility of other Prophet ﷺ descriptions. Ask: why do we call him 'Sayyid'?

• أَمَّا بَعْدُ appears in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī as something the Prophet ﷺ said in speeches. Mentioning this elevates its importance beyond just an author convention.

• Activity: Have students write this opening in their notebooks with full vowel marks. This is a calligraphy and Arabic writing exercise combined with memorization.

Al-Madrasatu An-Nuriyyah (AMAN)
Lesson 1 — Why Tawḥīd Comes First
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 3
Lesson 1 — Foundation
Tawḥīd Comes Before the Qur'ānقَبْلَ تَعْلِيمِهِمُ الْقُرْآنَ
The Author's Opening Principle — Page 8 (Must Memorize) عَلَى الإِنْسَانِ أَنْ يُعَلِّمَ الصِّبْيَانَ قَبْلَ تَعْلِيمِهِمُ الْقُرْآنَ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ مُسْلِمًا كَامِلًا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ الإِسْلَامِ وَمُوَحِّدًا جَيِّدًا عَلَى طَرِيقَةِ الإِيمَانِ "It is required to teach children Tawḥīd BEFORE the Qur'ān — so that they become a complete Muslim on the natural way of Islām, and a GOOD Muwaḥḥid on the path of true Īmān."
The Two Goals
  • ١
    مُسْلِمًا كَامِلًا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ الإِسْلَامِ A COMPLETE Muslim on the natural way (Fiṭrah) of Islām — standing firmly on the foundation Allāh built into every human heart
  • ٢
    مُوَحِّدًا جَيِّدًا عَلَى طَرِيقَةِ الإِيمَانِ A GOOD Muwaḥḥid on the path of Īmān — not just someone who says the words, but someone who genuinely believes with understanding
💡
جَيِّدًا = GOOD — This word is intentional. It's not enough to be a Muwaḥḥid in name only. The goal is to be a GOOD Muwaḥḥid — deep, genuine, and well-rooted.
The Method — سُؤَالٌ وَجَوَابٌ
وَرَتَّبْتُهُ عَلَى طَرِيقَةِ سُؤَالٍ وَجَوَابٍQuestion & Answer Format
"I have arranged it in the method of question and answer" — the author's words. This classical pedagogy forces active recall, not passive listening. The teacher asks — the student answers from memory.
🤔 Think & Write

Before we go further — write down in your own words: Why do you think knowing WHO Allāh is matters MORE than just reading His book? We'll come back to this.

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 3: Why Tawḥīd Before Qur'ān? — The Author's Statement

  • Read and memorize the full statement: عَلَى الإِنْسَانِ أَنْ يُعَلِّمَ الصِّبْيَانَ قَبْلَ تَعْلِيمِهِمُ الْقُرْآنَ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ مُسْلِمًا كَامِلًا.
  • Know the two goals: مُسْلِمًا كَامِلًا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ الإِسْلَامِ and مُوَحِّدًا جَيِّدًا عَلَى طَرِيقَةِ الإِيمَانِ.
  • Understand the significance of جَيِّدًا — not just any Muwaḥḥid, but a GOOD one.
  • Understand the سُؤَالٌ وَجَوَابٌ format and why the author chose it.
Read the full statement
Let's read the author's opening principle together — this is from page 8 of the book. [Read together three times, slowing down each time]. Now — what is he saying? He says it is REQUIRED — وَاجِبٌ — for every person to teach children Tawḥīd BEFORE the Qur'ān. Why? So they become two things: first — مُسْلِمًا كَامِلًا — a COMPLETE Muslim. Not a half-Muslim. Not a Muslim in name only. Complete. On the Fiṭrah — the natural way of Islām.
The second goal
Second goal: وَمُوَحِّدًا جَيِّدًا — a GOOD Muwaḥḥid. Notice the word جَيِّدًا — good. The author could have just said 'a Muwaḥḥid.' But he said 'a GOOD Muwaḥḥid.' Because it's possible to learn the words of Tawḥīd without truly understanding them. The goal is deep, genuine, well-rooted Tawḥīd — on the path of TRUE Īmān.
The format
And then he says: وَرَتَّبْتُهُ عَلَى طَرِيقَةِ سُؤَالٍ وَجَوَابٍ — 'I arranged it as question and answer.' This is how we study this book. I ask — you answer. This trains your mind to retrieve knowledge instantly — which is exactly what you'll need in the grave, in front of scholars, in front of your children one day.

Session 1 of 7

Week 1 — Final slide of session 1. ~15 min. Assign Q1 memorization for next week.

📋 7-week unit total: 1 session/week × ~60 min = ~7 hours. This slide = ~15 min.

⚠ Do NOT rush. It is better to finish 5 slides deeply than 10 slides superficially.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• Write the full principle on the board: …كَامِلًا عَلَى فِطْرَةِ الإِسْلَامِ وَمُوَحِّدًا جَيِّدًا — make students copy it with full vowel marks.

• The Fiṭrah concept (built-in feeling inside every person toward Allāh) is in the famous hadīth: كُلُّ مَوْلُودٍ يُولَدُ عَلَى الْفِطْرَةِ — 'Every child is born on the Fiṭrah.' Mention this connection.

• Analogy: Tawḥīd is the foundation of a house. The Qur'ān, prayer, fasting — these are the walls, roof, and furniture. A house without a foundation will collapse. Draw this on the board.

• The Q&A format mirrors how the Prophet ﷺ taught — Jibrīl ʿAS came in the form of a man and asked questions. This is the highest teaching tradition in Islām.

Al-Madrasatu An-Nuriyyah (AMAN)
Lesson 2 — Q1 & Q2: Who is Your Lord?
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 4
Lesson 2 — Knowing Allāh
Q1 & Q2: Who is Your Lord?مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ · وَمَا مَعْنَى الرَّبِّ؟
س ١إِذَا قِيلَ لَكَ: مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ — If asked: "Who is your Lord?"
Say: My Lord is Allāh — رَبِّيَ اللهُ
فَقُلْ: رَبِّيَ اللهُ
"Say: My Lord is Allāh." — This is also the first question asked in the grave by the angels!
س ٢وَمَا مَعْنَى «الرَّبُّ»؟ — What is the meaning of "Rabb"?
Say: The Owner, the One Worshipped — الْمَالِكُ الْمَعْبُودُ
فَقُلْ: الْمَالِكُ الْمَعْبُودُ
"The Owner and the One Worshipped."
Meaning of اللَّهُ — From the Text Page 9
Exact Text Wording وَمَعْنَى «اللهُ»: ذُو الأُلُوهِيَّةِ وَالْعُبُودِيَّةِ عَلَى خَلْقِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ "The meaning of 'Allāh' is: the One who has Ulūhiyyah and ʿUbūdiyyah over ALL of His creation."
الأُلُوهِيَّةُUlūhiyyah
The absolute right to be worshipped — belonging ONLY to Allāh
الْعُبُودِيَّةُʿUbūdiyyah
Complete being a servant — the status of every created being before Allāh
Rabb includes four meanings
  • 👑
    الْمَالِكُ — The OwnerAllāh owns everything in existence — nothing belongs to anyone else ultimately
  • 🌱
    الْخَالِقُ — The CreatorHe brought everything into existence from nothing
  • 🍽️
    الرَّازِقُ — The ProviderEvery morsel of food, every breath — provided by Allāh
  • 🙏
    الْمَعْبُودُ — The Only One WorshippedBecause He is Owner/Creator/Provider — ONLY He deserves worship

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 4: Q1 & Q2 — Who is Your Lord? / Meaning of Rabb

  • Memorize Q1: مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ → رَبِّيَ اللهُ — drill until instant.
  • Memorize Q2: وَمَا مَعْنَى الرَّبِّ؟ → الْمَالِكُ الْمَعْبُودُ.
  • Know the exact text meaning of Allāh: ذُو الأُلُوهِيَّةِ وَالْعُبُودِيَّةِ عَلَى خَلْقِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ.
  • Distinguish: الرَّبُّ = Owner + One Worshipped. اللهُ = One with Ulūhiyyah and ʿUbūdiyyah over ALL creation.
  • Know this is the first of the three grave questions.
Drill both Q&As — minimum 7 times
مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ [Class: رَبِّيَ اللهُ!]. Again: مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ [رَبِّيَ اللهُ!]. Now Q2: وَمَا مَعْنَى الرَّبِّ؟ [الْمَالِكُ الْمَعْبُودُ!]. Faster: وَمَا مَعْنَى الرَّبِّ؟ [الْمَالِكُ الْمَعْبُودُ!].
Explain الرَّبُّ
The text defines الرَّبُّ as: الْمَالِكُ الْمَعْبُودُ. Two words. Al-Mālik — the Owner. Al-Maʿbūd — the One Worshipped. Why are these two together? Because the Owner of everything has the RIGHT to be worshipped. If Allāh owns you, owns your breath, owns your life — then it makes perfect sense that only He deserves worship.
Explain اللهُ
And the text gives us the meaning of the Name 'Allāh' itself: وَمَعْنَى «اللهُ»: ذُو الأُلُوهِيَّةِ وَالْعُبُودِيَّةِ عَلَى خَلْقِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ — the One who has Ulūhiyyah — the right to be worshipped — and ʿUbūdiyyah — being fully a servant of Allāh — over ALL of His creation. Every single created being is in a state of ʿUbūdiyyah before Allāh. The trees, the stars, the angels, you, me — ALL of us.
Connect to the grave
Remember — the angels Munkar and Nakīr ask: مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ — 'Who is your Lord?' You've been practicing the answer since birth: رَبِّيَ اللهُ. But the question is — do you KNOW what you're saying? Now you do. Allāh is the Owner and the One Worshipped over all creation. That's your Lord.
⏱ Pacing Guide

Session 2 of 7

Week 2 — Begin with Q1 recall check (cold-call 5 students). ~25 min.

📋 7-week unit total: 1 session/week × ~60 min = ~7 hours. This slide = ~25 min.

⚠ Do NOT rush. It is better to finish 5 slides deeply than 10 slides superficially.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• Drill variations: call on individuals by name, whisper, shout, boys only, girls only, eyes closed — create muscle memory.

• Write الرَّبُّ = الْمَالِكُ + الْمَعْبُودُ on the board with an equals sign and a plus sign — visual logic.

• Ulūhiyyah and ʿUbūdiyyah are core ʿaqīdah vocabulary — introduce them here but revisit throughout the unit.

• The word 'Allāh' is not a translation — it is a proper name. The Arabic word for 'a god' is 'ilāh.' 'Al-Ilāh' becomes 'Allāh.' This etymology is important for deeper students.

Al-Madrasatu An-Nuriyyah (AMAN)
Lesson 2 — Q3: Signs of Allāh & Qur'ānic Proof
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 5
Lesson 2 — Knowing Allāh
Q3: How Do You Know Your Lord?بِمَ تَعْرِفُ رَبَّكَ؟
س ٣فَإِذَا قِيلَ لَكَ: بِمَ تَعْرِفُ رَبَّكَ؟ — How do you recognize your Lord?
Say: I recognize Him through His Signs and His Creation.
فَقُلْ: أَعْرِفُهُ بِآيَاتِهِ وَمَخْلُوقَاتِهِ
"I recognize Him through His signs (āyāt) and His creation (makhlūqāt)."
آيَاتُهُ — His Signs
اللَّيْلُ · وَالنَّهَارُ · الشَّمْسُ · وَالْقَمَرُNight · Day · Sun · Moon
مَخْلُوقَاتُهُ — His Creation
السَّمَاوَاتُ · وَالأَرْضُ · وَمَا فِيهِمَاThe Heavens · The Earth · Everything within them
📖 From the text exactly (Page 9):
وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ: اللَّيْلُ وَالنَّهَارُ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ
وَمِنْ مَخْلُوقَاتِهِ: السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالأَرْضُ وَمَا فِيهِمَا
The Dalīl — Sūrat Al-Aʿrāf 7:54 (Exact Text, Page 10)
Must Memorize — This is the Qur'ānic Proof إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ يَطْلُبُهُ حَثِيثًا تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ Sūrat Al-Aʿrāf · 7:54 "Indeed your Lord is Allāh who created the heavens and earth in six days, then rose above the Throne, covering the night with the day rapidly… Blessed is Allāh, Lord of the worlds."
Youth Educated… Family Cultivated… World Illuminated amanschoolmn.org · amanschool.mn@gmail.com

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 5: Q3 — How Do You Know Your Lord? + Dalīl Al-Aʿrāf 7:54

  • Memorize Q3: بِمَ تَعْرِفُ رَبَّكَ؟ → أَعْرِفُهُ بِآيَاتِهِ وَمَخْلُوقَاتِهِ.
  • Know the exact Arabic from the text: ومن آياته: الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر / ومن مخلوقاته: السماوات والأرض وما فيهما.
  • Begin memorizing Al-Aʿrāf 7:54 — at minimum the first and last phrases.
  • Know the meaning of each phrase in Al-Aʿrāf 54: creation in 6 days, istawā ʿalā al-ʿarsh, night covering day, Rabb al-ʿālamīn.
Drill Q3
Q3: بِمَ تَعْرِفُ رَبَّكَ؟ [Class: أَعْرِفُهُ بِآيَاتِهِ وَمَخْلُوقَاتِهِ!]. Again [repeat 5x]. Now in English: How do you recognize your Lord? [Through His signs and His creation!].
What are the signs?
The text says: وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ — from His SIGNS: اللَّيْلُ وَالنَّهَارُ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ — night, day, sun, moon. And from His CREATION: السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالأَرْضُ وَمَا فِيهِمَا — the heavens, the earth, everything within them. Look outside right now — every single thing you see is either a sign or a creation of Allāh pointing to His existence and power.
The Dalīl — Al-Aʿrāf 54
The author then gives us the Dalīl — the Qur'ānic proof. Al-Aʿrāf verse 54: إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ — 'Indeed YOUR Lord is Allāh who created the heavens and earth in SIX DAYS.' Allāh could have done it in a second — He chose six days, showing intentional, deliberate creation. ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ — then He rose above the Throne. يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ — He covers the night with the day. And the conclusion: تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ — Blessed is Allāh, Lord of ALL the worlds.
Connect Q3 to the āyah
Do you see the connection? The āyah proves the answer to Q3! How do we know Allāh? His signs — the āyah mentions night, day. His creation — the āyah mentions heavens and earth. And then تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ — He is the Lord of the worlds. Q3 answered by the Qur'ān directly.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• Go outside briefly (weather permitting) and ask students to identify signs and creations of Allāh — make the lesson experiential.

• Al-Aʿrāf 54 contains important ʿaqīdah: istawā ʿalā al-ʿarsh (rising above the Throne) is an attribute we believe without asking 'how' — bilā kayf. Mention this to older students.

• The āyah mentions that the sun and moon are 'subjected by His command' — this is an argument against sun/moon worship, connecting back to the Signs vs. Creation distinction.

• Have students play 'signs or creation?' — point at things in the room and have them categorize: the window (creation), sunlight coming through (sign), a plant (creation)…

Lesson 3 — Q4: Why Were We Created?
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله

Lesson 3 — Purpose of Creation
Q4: Why Did Allāh Create You?لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَكَ؟
س ٤فَإِنْ قِيلَ: لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَكَ؟ — For what purpose did Allāh create you?
Say: For His worship alone — with no partner — obeying what He commands and leaving what He forbids.
فَقُلْ: لِعِبَادَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ
بِامْتِثَالِ مَا أَمَرَ بِهِ، وَتَرْكِ مَا نَهَى عَنْهُ
"To worship Him alone, with no partner — obeying His commands and leaving His prohibitions."
وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ
Sūrat Al-Dhāriyāt · 51:56
"And I did not create the Jinn and Mankind except to worship Me."
وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا
Sūrat An-Nisāʾ · 4:36
"Worship Allāh and associate nothing with Him."
What Does ʿIbādah Mean? — Page 12
The Complete Definition — Must Memorize فَإِنَّ الْعِبَادَةَ: اسْمٌ جَامِعٌ لِكُلِّ مَا يُحِبُّهُ اللهُ وَيَرْضَاهُ مِنَ الأَقْوَالِ وَالأَعْمَالِ الْبَاطِنَةِ وَالظَّاهِرَةِ "ʿIbādah is a a word that covers everything Allāh loves — from statements and inward and outward actions."
الأَقْوَالُ
Statements
Shahādah, Dhikr, Duʿāʾ, Qur'ān recitation
الأَعْمَالُ الظَّاهِرَةُ
Outward Actions
Prayer, Fasting, Ḥajj, Zakāh, Charity
الأَعْمَالُ الْبَاطِنَةُ
Inward Actions
Love, Fear, Hope, Trust, Sincerity — of the HEART
الشَّرْطُ — Condition
Must be for Allāh alone + following the Prophet ﷺ

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 6: Q4 — Why Were You Created? + Definition of ʿIbādah

  • Memorize Q4: لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَكَ؟ → لِعِبَادَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ · بِامْتِثَالِ مَا أَمَرَ بِهِ وَتَرْكِ مَا نَهَى عَنْهُ.
  • Memorize the ʿIbādah definition: اسْمٌ جَامِعٌ لِكُلِّ مَا يُحِبُّهُ اللهُ وَيَرْضَاهُ مِنَ الأَقْوَالِ وَالأَعْمَالِ الْبَاطِنَةِ وَالظَّاهِرَةِ.
  • Know Al-Dhāriyāt 51:56 and An-Nisāʾ 4:36 as the Qur'ānic proofs.
  • Know the three categories: statements (tongue), outward actions (body), inward actions (heart).
Drill Q4
لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَكَ؟ [Class: لِعِبَادَتِهِ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ!]. The answer from the text adds: بِامْتِثَالِ مَا أَمَرَ بِهِ وَتَرْكِ مَا نَهَى عَنْهُ — by obeying what He commands and leaving what He forbids. This tells us what worship LOOKS LIKE in practice: obedience plus avoidance.
Al-Dhāriyāt 56 — the most important verse on purpose
Allāh says in the Qur'ān — and this is the most direct statement of human purpose ever given: وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ — 'I did not create the Jinn and Mankind EXCEPT to worship Me.' No other purpose is mentioned. Everything else — your career, family, health, talents — exists WITHIN this purpose. You fulfill your purpose when you worship Allāh with everything you have.
The definition of ʿIbādah
So what IS ʿIbādah? The text gives a comprehensive definition: اسْمٌ جَامِعٌ — a COMPREHENSIVE name. Not limited to prayer. Not just the mosque. It covers: الأَقْوَالُ — things you SAY. الأَعْمَالُ الظَّاهِرَةُ — things you DO with your body. And the most forgotten category: الأَعْمَالُ الْبَاطِنَةُ — things inside your HEART. Love for Allāh, fear of Allāh, hope in Allāh — these are worship.
Practical application
When you eat breakfast and say Bismillah — that's ʿIbādah. When you help your mom and your intention is to please Allāh — ʿIbādah. When you feel gratitude in your heart for a beautiful sunrise — ʿIbādah. Your ENTIRE life can be worship if your intention is for Allāh.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• Al-Dhāriyāt 56 is arguably the most important verse in the Qur'ān for understanding human purpose. Spend serious time on it.

• The definition 'اسم جامع' comes originally from Ibn Taymiyyah's formulation — the author is citing scholarly tradition, not inventing it. This shows the depth behind the simple-seeming text.

• Activity: Give students 2 minutes to list 10 acts of worship. Then categorize together: which are tongue (قول)? Body (ظاهر)? Heart (باطن)?

• The two conditions for ʿIbādah to be accepted — Ikhlāṣ (sincerity) and Ittibāʿ (following the Prophet ﷺ) — come from Sūrat Al-Bayyinah 98:5 and are implied in 'وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ'. Mention for older students.

Lesson 4 — Shirk: The Greatest Sin
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 7
Lesson 4 — Shirk
Shirk — Allāh's Greatest Prohibitionوَالشِّرْكُ أَعْظَمُ ذَنْبٍ عُصِيَ اللهُ بِهِ
⚠️
وَالشِّرْكُ أَعْظَمُ ذَنْبٍ عُصِيَ اللهُ بِهِ "Shirk is the greatest sin by which Allāh is disobeyed." — From the Text, Page 11
The Definition of Shirk — Exact Text Page 12
Full Definition — Pages 11–12 وَالشِّرْكُ: أَنْ يَجْعَلَ لِلَّهِ نِدًّا يَدْعُوهُ، أَوْ يَرْجُوهُ، أَوْ يَخَافُهُ أَوْ يَتَوَكَّلُ عَلَيْهِ، أَوْ يَرْغَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ، وَغَيْرُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْوَاعِ الْعِبَادَاتِ "Shirk is to give Allāh a rival (Nidd) — that one calls upon, hopes in, fears, relies upon, or desires from besides Allāh — and other forms of worship directed elsewhere."
إِنَّهُ مَن يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْجَنَّةَ وَمَأْوَاهُ النَّارُ وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنصَارٍ
Sūrat Al-Māʾidah · 5:72
"Whoever commits Shirk — Allāh has forbidden him Paradise and his home is the Fire. And the wrongdoers will have no helpers."
The Five Acts of Shirk — All Must Be for Allāh Only
  • 🤲
    الدُّعَاءُ — Calling/SupplicationيَدْعُوهُMaking duʿāʾ to other than Allāh = Shirk
  • 🌟
    الرَّجَاءُ — Hopeأَوْ يَرْجُوهُPlacing hope in other than Allāh for help = Shirk
  • 😨
    الْخَوْفُ — Fearأَوْ يَخَافُهُFearing other than Allāh as one fears Allāh = Shirk
  • 🤝
    التَّوَكُّلُ — Relianceأَوْ يَتَوَكَّلُ عَلَيْهِTrusting/relying on other than Allāh = Shirk
  • ❤️
    الرَّغْبَةُ — Desire/Loveأَوْ يَرْغَبُ إِلَيْهِDirecting love/desire to other than Allāh = Shirk
وَلَقَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكَ لَئِن أَشْرَكْتَ لَيَحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ وَلَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ — بَلِ اللَّهَ فَاعْبُدْ وَكُن مِّنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ
Az-Zumar · 39:65 — Even the Prophet ﷺ was warned: Shirk nullifies ALL deeds!

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 7: Shirk — The Greatest Sin · Full Definition from Text

  • Memorize the key statement: وَالشِّرْكُ أَعْظَمُ ذَنْبٍ عُصِيَ اللهُ بِهِ.
  • Memorize the full definition: أَنْ يَجْعَلَ لِلَّهِ نِدًّا يَدْعُوهُ أَوْ يَرْجُوهُ أَوْ يَخَافُهُ أَوْ يَتَوَكَّلُ عَلَيْهِ أَوْ يَرْغَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ.
  • Know Al-Māʾidah 5:72 and Az-Zumar 39:65 as proofs.
  • Know the five acts that constitute Shirk when directed to other than Allāh: duʿāʾ, hope, fear, reliance, desire.
Establish gravity
We need to talk about the most dangerous thing a Muslim can fall into. The text says clearly: وَالشِّرْكُ أَعْظَمُ ذَنْبٍ عُصِيَ اللهُ بِهِ — 'Shirk is the GREATEST sin by which Allāh is disobeyed.' Greater than murder. Greater than lying. Greater than any other sin. Why? Because Shirk attacks the very core of what we believe — that Allāh is ONE.
The exact definition
The author defines Shirk precisely: أَنْ يَجْعَلَ لِلَّهِ نِدًّا — to give Allāh a RIVAL. A Nidd — نِدٌّ — is an equal, a rival, someone on the same level. Shirk means treating something as EQUAL to Allāh in acts of worship. And the text lists FIVE forms: calling upon (duʿāʾ), hoping in, fearing, relying upon, desiring from — any of these directed to other than Allāh while the person could direct it to Allāh is Shirk.
The consequence — Al-Māʾidah 72
Allāh says in the Qur'ān — and these words should shake us: إِنَّهُ مَن يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْجَنَّةَ وَمَأْوَاهُ النَّارُ — whoever commits Shirk, Allāh has made Paradise FORBIDDEN for him, and his home is the Fire. The word ḥarrama — حَرَّمَ — means absolutely forbidden, sealed shut. And his home — not just a visit — but his permanent dwelling — is the Fire.
Nullifies all deeds — Az-Zumar 65
And Az-Zumar 65 — Allāh said this to the PROPHET ﷺ himself to show us: لَئِن أَشْرَكْتَ لَيَحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ — 'If you commit Shirk, all your good deeds will be completely WIPED OUT.' Gone. Finished. Every prayer, every fast, every kind act — wiped out by Shirk. This is why protecting Tawḥīd is the most urgent task of a Muslim's life.

⚠ Do NOT rush. It is better to finish 5 slides deeply than 10 slides superficially.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• This is the most important warning in the book — give it the weight it deserves, without creating anxiety. The antidote to Shirk is LEARNING about it, which is exactly what they're doing.

• The five forms of Shirk in the definition (duʿāʾ, rajāʾ, khawf, tawakkul, raghbah) are exactly the five heart-worship acts from Lesson 3's ʿIbādah definition — they must ONLY go to Allāh.

• Age-appropriate examples: going to fortune tellers/horoscopes (hope in other), wearing amulets for protection (relying on other), believing evil eye charms protect (fear of other-than-Allāh).

• Pastoral note: some students may realize their families practice things that are Shirk. Handle with great care — emphasize that learning about Shirk is how you PROTECT yourself, and that Allāh accepts repentance.

Lesson 5 — Duʿāʾ: The Heart of Worship
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 8
Lesson 5 — Duʿāʾ
Duʿāʾ — The Heart of Worshipالدُّعَاءُ مِنْ أَعْظَمِ أَنْوَاعِ الْعِبَادَاتِ
From the Text — Page 13 (Exact Wording)
Text Statement + Hadīth وَمِنْهَا: الدُّعَاءُ وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ الدُّعَاءَ مِنْ أَعْظَمِ أَنْوَاعِ الْعِبَادَاتِ وَفِي «السُّنَنِ»: عَنْ أَنَسٍ مَرْفُوعًا: الدُّعَاءُ مُخُّ الْعِبَادَةِ At-Tirmidhī 3371 — graded weak (ḍaʿīf) by al-Albānī, Ḍaʿīf al-Jāmiʿ 303 "And from it (worship) is: Duʿāʾ. And that is because Duʿāʾ is from the GREATEST forms of worship. Duʿāʾ is the HEART AND SOUL of worship." وَيُغْنِي عَنْهُ: الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ The authentic wording — Aḥmad 18378 · graded ṣaḥīḥ by al-Albānī, Ṣaḥīḥ al-Jāmiʿ 3407 The stronger, authentic narration: "Duʿāʾ IS worship" — use this wording with confidence.
وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلَا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَدًا
Sūrat Al-Jinn · 72:18
"The masjids are for Allāh — so do not call upon anyone along with Allāh."
وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ
Sūrat Ghāfir · 40:60
"Your Lord said: 'Call upon Me — I will respond. Those too proud to worship Me will enter Hell humiliated.'"
Calling Upon Other Than Allāh is Kufr
Key Heading from Page 13 الدَّلِيلُ عَلَى أَنَّ دَعْوَةَ غَيْرِ اللهِ كُفْرٌ "The proof that calling upon other than Allāh is Kufr (disbelief)"
وَالدَّلِيلُ عَلَى أَنَّ دَعْوَةَ غَيْرِ اللهِ كُفْرٌ — وَمَن يَدْعُ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ لَا بُرْهَانَ لَهُ بِهِ فَإِنَّمَا حِسَابُهُ عِندَ رَبِّهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ
Sūrat Al-Muʾminūn · 23:117
"Whoever calls upon another god alongside Allāh — for which he has no proof — his reckoning is with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed."
🚫
Three rulings on Duʿāʾ:
✅ Duʿāʾ to Allāh = the greatest worship
⚠️ No Duʿāʾ to Allāh = arrogance (Ghāfir 60)
❌ Duʿāʾ to other than Allāh = Kufr (Al-Muʾminūn 117)
🤲 Let's Make Duʿāʾ Now

اللَّهُمَّ أَرِنَا الْحَقَّ حَقًّا وَارْزُقْنَا اتِّبَاعَهُ · وَأَرِنَا الْبَاطِلَ بَاطِلًا وَارْزُقْنَا اجْتِنَابَهُ
O Allāh, show us truth as truth and give us the ability to follow it — and show us falsehood as falsehood and give us the ability to avoid it. Āmīn.

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 8: Duʿāʾ is the Heart of Worship — Three Qur'ānic Proofs

  • Know the exact text statement: الدُّعَاءُ مِنْ أَعْظَمِ أَنْوَاعِ الْعِبَادَاتِ and the hadīth: الدُّعَاءُ مُخُّ الْعِبَادَةِ.
  • Know Al-Jinn 72:18, Ghāfir 40:60, and Al-Muʾminūn 23:117.
  • Know the text heading: الدَّلِيلُ عَلَى أَنَّ دَعْوَةَ غَيْرِ اللهِ كُفْرٌ.
  • Know the three rulings: duʿāʾ to Allāh = worship; no duʿāʾ = arrogance; duʿāʾ to other = Kufr.
  • Memorize the duʿāʾ: اللَّهُمَّ أَرِنَا الْحَقَّ حَقًّا...
Why duʿāʾ?
The text says: وَمِنْهَا: الدُّعَاءُ — and from ʿIbādah is DUʿĀĀ. And then it makes a powerful statement: وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ الدُّعَاءَ مِنْ أَعْظَمِ أَنْوَاعِ الْعِبَادَاتِ — 'This is because duʿāʾ is from the GREATEST forms of worship.' Why greatest? Because when you make duʿāʾ you are showing complete dependency on Allāh. You're saying: I cannot do this alone. I need YOU. That's the height of being a servant.
The Hadīth — مُخُّ الْعِبَادَةِ
And the Prophet ﷺ said: الدُّعَاءُ مُخُّ الْعِبَادَةِ — 'Duʿāʾ is the HEART AND SOUL of worship.' مُخٌّ means the deepest, most important post vital part. Cut it out and the bone dies. Similarly, duʿāʾ is the deepest, most essential core of worship.
Three āyāt
Three evidence from Qur'ān: First — Al-Jinn 18: وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلَا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَدًا — 'The masjids are for ALLĀH — so do not call on anyone WITH Allāh.' The holiest places — the masjids — Allāh specified: NO duʿāʾ except to Me. Second — Ghāfir 60: Allāh COMMANDS us: ادْعُونِي — 'Call upon ME!' He says He WILL respond. And those too proud to make duʿāʾ will enter Hell HUMILIATED. Third — Al-Muʾminūn 117: calling upon another god alongside Allāh — the disbelievers will NOT succeed.
Make duʿāʾ as a class
Now let's practice what we just learned. We're going to make duʿāʾ to Allāh ALONE — right now. [Lead the class in the duʿāʾ: اللَّهُمَّ أَرِنَا الْحَقَّ حَقًّا...] — That was worship. That was the heart and soul of ʿIbādah.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• The text footnote notes that 'الدعاء مخ العبادة' has two chains — one weak (Tirmidhī 3371, graded weak by Al-Albānī in Ḍaʿīf al-Jāmiʿ 3003) and the stronger wording 'الدعاء هو العبادة' (Aḥmad 18378, graded ṣaḥīḥ in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Jāmiʿ 3407). Always use the stronger narration.

• Ghāfir 60 says NOT making duʿāʾ to Allāh leads to hellfire 'humiliated' — this is a sobering reminder that arrogance in worship is dangerous.

• The text's heading 'الدليل على أن دعوة غير الله كفر' — is a title the author uses, showing he systematically proves each point. Teach students to see the structure of Islamic argumentation.

• End every Tawḥīd class with duʿāʾ — model what you teach. The class duʿāʾ above (اللهم أرنا الحق حقاً) is perfect for the Tawḥīd unit.

Lesson 5 — More Types of Worship from the Heart
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Pages 14–15 · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 8B
Lesson 5
Heart Worship — 5 More Types of ʿIbādah أَنْوَاعُ الْعِبَادَةِ الْقَلْبِيَّةِ
From the Text — Pages 14–15 (Exact Wording)
  • ١
    الْخَوْفُ — Fear of Allāh وَمِنْهَا: الْخَوْفُ Being scared of Allāh the way He deserves — only Allāh should be feared in our hearts this way
  • ٢
    الرَّجَاءُ — Hope in Allāh وَمِنْهَا: الرَّجَاءُ Hoping for Allāh's reward and mercy — your heart turns to HIM when you want good things
  • ٣
    التَّوَكُّلُ — Trusting Allāh وَمِنْهَا: التَّوَكُّلُ Putting your full trust in Allāh — you do your part, then rely on HIM for the result
  • ٤
    الرَّغْبَةُ وَالرَّهْبَةُ — Desire & Awe وَمِنْهَا: الرَّغْبَةُ وَالرَّهْبَةُ Wanting Allāh's reward (raghbah) and being in awe of His power (rahbah)
  • ٥
    الإِنَابَةُ — Turning Back to Allāh وَمِنْهَا: الإِنَابَةُ Turning your heart back to Allāh when you make a mistake — He is always ready to accept you
The Qur'ānic Proofs — From the Text
إِنَّمَا ذَلِكُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِيَاءَهُ فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمْ وَخَافُونِ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
Āl ʿImrān · 3:175 — Proof for Khawf
"Shayṭān only tries to scare you with his friends — so don't be scared of THEM. Be scared of ME — if you are truly believers."
فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُو لِقَاءَ رَبِّهِ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِ أَحَدًا
Al-Kahf · 18:110 — Proof for Rajāʾ
"Whoever hopes to meet their Lord — do good deeds and don't share anyone in worshipping your Lord."
وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوا إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ
Al-Māʾidah · 5:23 + Al-Ṭalāq · 65:3 — Proof for Tawakkul
"Trust in Allāh — if you are believers." · "Whoever trusts in Allāh, He is enough for them."
إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا وَكَانُوا لَنَا خَاشِعِينَ
Al-Anbiyāʾ · 21:90 — Proof for Raghbah & Rahbah
"They rushed to do good things and called on Us with hope and awe — and they were humble before Us."
💡
KEY RULE: All five of these — fear, hope, trust, desire, turning back — are acts of WORSHIP. If they go to other than Allāh, that is SHIRK. They belong to Allāh alone!

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 8B: Heart Worship

  • Know all 5 heart-worship types with Arabic names: الْخَوْفُ · الرَّجَاءُ · التَّوَكُّلُ · الرَّغْبَةُ وَالرَّهْبَةُ · الإِنَابَةُ
  • Know the dalīl for each from the text (Āl ʿImrān 3:175, Al-Kahf 18:110, Al-Māʾidah 5:23, Al-Anbiyāʾ 21:90)
  • Understand the key rule: all five directed to other than Allāh = Shirk
  • Connect to the definition of ʿIbādah: these are all "inward acts" (الأَعْمَالُ الْبَاطِنَةُ)
Set up the heart connection
We talked about what worship IS — a word that covers everything Allāh loves. Today we go DEEPER into the heart. Because worship isn't just what you DO with your body. What happens INSIDE your heart matters too. The book lists five heart-worship acts that ONLY Allāh deserves.
Walk through each type simply
First: الْخَوْفُ — fear. There's a normal fear — like being scared of a dog that might bite you. That's fine. But the SPECIAL fear — the deep fear in your heart that makes you obey — that belongs only to Allāh. Allāh says in the Qur'ān: "Don't be scared of Shayṭān's friends — be scared of ME." If someone fears a saint or a dead person the way they should fear Allāh — that's Shirk.
Second: الرَّجَاءُ — hope. When you want something — a good grade, to get better when you're sick, to go to Jannah — where does your heart go? To Allāh. Hope in Allāh means your heart reaches toward HIM for good things. Allāh says: if you hope to meet your Lord — do good deeds and don't share anyone with Him in worship.
Third: التَّوَكُّلُ — trusting Allāh. This one trips many people up. Tawakkul doesn't mean you sit and do nothing. You TIE YOUR CAMEL FIRST — meaning you do everything in your power — then you trust Allāh for the result. You study for the test AND trust Allāh. You take the medicine AND trust Allāh. Trusting only the camel — without Allāh — is Shirk.
Four and five are الرَّغْبَةُ — wanting Allāh's good things — and الرَّهْبَةُ — being in awe of His power. And then الإِنَابَةُ — turning back to Allāh. This one is beautiful. Every time you make a mistake — you turn back to Allāh. He is always waiting. وَأَنِيبُوا إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ — turn back to your Lord.

Lesson 6 — The Ṭāghūt: What to Reject
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 9
Lesson 6 — Ṭāghūt
First Obligation: Reject the Ṭāghūtالْكُفْرُ بِالطَّاغُوتِ وَالإِيمَانُ بِاللَّهِ
The First Obligation — Page 15 وَأَوَّلُ مَا فَرَضَ اللهُ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ: الْكُفْرُ بِالطَّاغُوتِ وَالإِيمَانُ بِاللَّهِ "The FIRST thing Allāh required from His servants: Rejection of the Ṭāghūt AND Belief in Allāh."
وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولًا أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاجْتَنِبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ
Sūrat An-Naḥl · 16:36
"We sent a Messenger to every nation: WORSHIP ALLĀH and AVOID THE ṬĀGHŪT." — This was every prophet's message!
الطَّاغُوتُDefinition from Text — Page 15
مَا عُبِدَ مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ "Whatever is worshipped besides Allāh" — including:

① الشَّيْطَانُ — Shayṭān
② الْكِهَانَةُ — Fortune-telling/Soothsaying
③ الْمُنَجِّمُ — Astrologers
④ مَنْ يَحْكُمُ بِغَيْرِ مَا أَنزَلَ اللهُ — Those who rule by other than Allāh's law
⑤ كُلُّ مَتْبُوعٍ مُطَاعٍ عَلَى غَيْرِ الْحَقِّ — Any leader obeyed against the truth
Ibn al-Qayyim's Definition — Exact Text Page 16
قَالَ الْعَلَّامَةُ ابْنُ الْقَيِّمِ رَحِمَهُ اللهُ تَعَالَى:
الطَّاغُوتُ: مَا تَجَاوَزَ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ حَدَّهُ مِنْ مَعْبُودٍ، أَوْ مَتْبُوعٍ، أَوْ مُطَاعٍ
Ibn al-Qayyim رحمه الله · Iʿlām al-Muwaqiʿīn 1/5
"Ṭāghūt is whatever a person goes too far with — whether it is something worshipped, followed, or obeyed."
مَعْبُودٌWorshipped
Praying to, making duʿāʾ to, seeking help from anything other than Allāh
مَتْبُوعٌFollowed
Following a person, ideology, or system that contradicts Allāh's commands
مُطَاعٌObeyed
Obeying someone in disobedience to Allāh — making their word supreme
💡
Two steps ALWAYS go together:
① الْكُفْرُ بِالطَّاغُوتِ — REJECT the Ṭāghūt first
② الإِيمَانُ بِاللَّهِ — THEN believe in Allāh
Just like the Shahādah: لَا إِلَهَ (reject) + إِلَّا اللهُ (affirm)

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 9: First Obligation: Kufr bi al-Ṭāghūt · Full Definition

  • Memorize: وَأَوَّلُ مَا فَرَضَ اللهُ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ: الْكُفْرُ بِالطَّاغُوتِ وَالإِيمَانُ بِاللَّهِ.
  • Know An-Naḥl 16:36 — the universal message of ALL prophets.
  • Know the text's definition of Ṭāghūt and its five categories (pages 15).
  • Know Ibn al-Qayyim's precise definition: مَعْبُودٌ · مَتْبُوعٌ · مُطَاعٌ.
  • Understand why rejection (Kufr bi al-Ṭāghūt) MUST come before the YES part (Īmān bi Allāh).
The first obligation
Before belief in Allāh comes something. The text says: وَأَوَّلُ مَا فَرَضَ اللهُ — the FIRST thing required. Not prayer. Not fasting. Not kindness to parents. The FIRST obligation: الْكُفْرُ بِالطَّاغُوتِ — REJECTION of the Ṭāghūt. Then — وَالإِيمَانُ بِاللَّهِ — belief in Allāh. Rejection comes FIRST. Why? Because valid Tawḥīd requires two parts: تَبَرُّء — rejection of the false — and إِيمَان — belief in the true. Like the Shahādah: لَا إِلَهَ first (rejection), then إِلَّا اللهُ (the YES part).
Define Ṭāghūt from the text
What is the Ṭāghūt? The text says: مَا عُبِدَ مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ — whatever is worshipped besides Allāh. And then gives specific examples: Shayṭān (the original Ṭāghūt), fortune tellers, astrologers, those who rule by other than Allāh's law, anyone followed against the truth. Any of these is a Ṭāghūt.
Ibn al-Qayyim's definition
And Ibn al-Qayyim gives us the most precise definition — which the author quotes directly: الطَّاغُوتُ مَا تَجَاوَزَ بِهِ الْعَبْدُ حَدَّهُ — 'Ṭāghūt is whatever a person goes too far with.' Three forms: worshipped (like an idol), followed (like a false guide), or obeyed (like a tyrant). The word Ṭāghūt comes from the root طَغَى — to go too far, to go beyond limits. When something crosses the line into the territory of Allāh — that's Ṭāghūt.
An-Naḥl 36 — universal message
And An-Naḥl 36 shows this was ALWAYS the message: وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولًا — 'We sent to every nation a messenger.' Every. Nation. Every prophet. Same message: اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاجْتَنِبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ — worship Allāh and AVOID the Ṭāghūt. Nūḥ ﷺ said it. Ibrāhīm ﷺ. Mūsā ﷺ. ʿĪsā ﷺ. Our Prophet ﷺ. One message, forever.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• The root طَغَى means to go beyond limits — like water flooding beyond its banks. Ṭāghūt is something that floods beyond its proper place into the territory of Allāh.

• Ibn al-Qayyim's reference (Iʿlām al-Muwaqiʿīn 1/5) is in the book's actual footnote — this is a scholarly citation inside a children's book, showing its depth.

• The connection: Ṭāghūt must be rejected BEFORE Allāh is affirmed — exactly parallels the Shahādah structure (Nafī before Ithbāt). Diagram this side-by-side on the board.

• Age-appropriate Ṭāghūt examples: checking horoscopes (following astrology), wearing amulets (worshipping/relying on other than Allāh), obeying someone in disobeying parents/deen (obeying a Ṭāghūt).

Q5: What is Your Religion?مَا دِينُكَ؟ · دِينِيَ الإِسْلَامُ
س ٥فَإِنْ قِيلَ لَكَ: مَا دِينُكَ؟ — What is your religion?
Say: My religion is Islām.

"Say: My religion is Islām." — The second of the three grave questions.
Meaning of Islām — Exact Text Pages 16–17
Four-Part Definition — Must Memorize مَعْنَى الإِسْلَامِ: الاسْتِسْلَامُ لِلَّهِ بِالتَّوْحِيدِ وَالانْقِيَادُ لَهُ بِالطَّاعَةِ وَمُوَالاةُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَمُعَادَاةُ الْمُشْرِكِينَ Surrendering to Allāh with Tawḥīd · Submitting to Him in obedience · Loyalty to the Muslims · Rejection of the people who worship false gods
إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ اللَّهِ الإِسْلَامُ
Āl ʿImrān · 3:19
"Indeed, the religion that Allāh accepts is Islām."
وَمَن يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الإِسْلَامِ دِينًا فَلَن يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ
Āl ʿImrān · 3:85
"Whoever seeks a religion other than Islām — it will never be accepted from him."
Hadīth of Jibrīl — The Prophet's ﷺ Definition
وَصَحَّ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «الإِسْلَامُ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ، وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللهِ، وَتُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةَ، وَتُؤْتِيَ الزَّكَاةَ، وَتَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ، وَتَحُجَّ الْبَيْتَ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا»
Al-Bukhārī 4777 · Muslim 102 — Ṣaḥīḥ
"Islām is to testify there is no god but Allāh and Muḥammad is His Messenger; to establish prayer; to give Zakāh; to fast Ramaḍān; and to perform Ḥajj if able."
الاسْتِسْلَامُSurrender
Complete surrender to Allāh with Tawḥīd — no resistance, no conditions
الانْقِيَادُSubmission
Full submission in obedience to Allāh's commands — not just belief but ACTION
مُوَالَاةٌLoyalty
Love and loyalty to the Muslims — you are one Ummah
مُعَادَاةٌRejecting False Gods
Staying away from the beliefs of people who worship false gods — not hating people, but rejecting Shirk

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 10: Q5 — What is Your Religion? + Meaning of Islām

  • Memorize Q5: مَا دِينُكَ؟ → دِينِيَ الإِسْلَامُ.
  • Memorize the four-part definition of Islām: الاسْتِسْلَامُ · الانْقِيَادُ · مُوَالاةُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ · مُعَادَاةُ الْمُشْرِكِينَ.
  • Know Āl ʿImrān 3:19 and 3:85.
  • Know the Hadīth of Jibrīl's definition of Islām (Al-Bukhārī 4777, Muslim 102).
Drill Q5
Q5: مَا دِينُكَ؟ [Class: دِينِيَ الإِسْلَامُ!]. Again and again. Now — what does Islām MEAN? Not just the name — the definition.
Four-part definition
The text gives four parts to the meaning of Islām. First: الاسْتِسْلَامُ لِلَّهِ بِالتَّوْحِيدِ — surrendering to Allāh with Tawḥīd. Complete surrender — no resistance. Second: الانْقِيَادُ لَهُ بِالطَّاعَةِ — submitting to Him in obedience. Not just believing, but DOING. Third: وَمُوَالاةُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ — loyalty and love for the Muslims. We are one Ummah. Fourth: وَمُعَادَاةُ الْمُشْرِكِينَ — reject and stay away froming the people who worship false gods. NOT hating people — but rejecting their Shirk and its beliefs.
The Qur'ānic proof
Allāh says in Āl ʿImrān 19: إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ اللَّهِ الإِسْلَامُ — THE religion with Allāh IS Islām. THE. Not one of many. And verse 85: whoever seeks OTHER than Islām as a religion — it will NEVER be accepted. This is not our opinion — it's Allāh's own statement.
The Hadīth of Jibrīl
The Prophet ﷺ defined Islām when the angel Jibrīl came in human form and asked him. He said: الإِسْلَامُ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ... — five things. This is the Hadīth of Jibrīl, recorded in both Al-Bukhārī and Muslim. The text quotes it directly. These five are the Five Pillars — the practical structure of Islām.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• The four-part definition of Islām (istislām, inqiyād, muwālāt, muʿādāt) is sophisticated — take time on each word.

• مُعَادَاةُ الْمُشْرِكِينَ needs careful explanation for children: this means rejecting and disowning the BELIEFS and PRACTICES of Shirk — not being unkind to non-Muslim people. Allāh commands justice with peaceful non-Muslims.

• The Hadīth of Jibrīl is called 'Abu al-Sunnah' — the Father of the Sunnah — because it encompasses the entire structure of the religion (Islām, Īmān, Iḥsān). The text references it here for the Islām portion.

• Now drill all three grave Q&As together rapidly: مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ / مَا دِينُكَ؟ / مَنْ نَبِيُّكَ؟ — students should answer all three without hesitation by now.

  • ١
    Ash-Shahādah — الشَّهَادَةُ أَنْ تَشْهَدَ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللهِ To testify there is no god worthy of worship but Allāh and Muḥammad ﷺ is His Messenger — the Foundation

    Aṣ-Ṣawm — الصِّيَامُ · وَتَصُومَ رَمَضَانَ Fasting the month of Ramaḍān · Proof below ↓

    Al-Ḥajj — الْحَجُّ · وَتَحُجَّ الْبَيْتَ إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا Pilgrimage to the Kaʿbah if able · Proof below ↓
Dalīl for Fasting — Pages 20–21
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ
شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَاتٍ مِّنَ الْهُدَى وَالْفُرْقَانِ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ
Sūrat Al-Baqarah · 2:183–185
"O believers, fasting has been prescribed upon you as it was prescribed upon those before you… Ramaḍān is the month in which the Qur'ān was revealed… whoever witnesses the month must fast it."
Dalīl for Ḥajj — Page 21
وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا
Āl ʿImrān · 3:97
"And Ḥajj to the House is a duty for all people for Allāh — for whoever is able to find a way."

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 11: Five Pillars of Islām + Evidences for Fasting & Ḥajj

  • Know all Five Pillars with their Arabic names and Qur'ānic evidences.
  • Memorize Al-Baqarah 2:183 and 185 as evidence for fasting.
  • Memorize Āl ʿImrān 3:97 as evidence for Ḥajj.
  • Know Al-Bayyinah 98:5 as evidence for Ṣalāh and Zakāh.
  • Know the greatest command and prohibition: فَأَعْظَمُ مَا أَمَرَ بِهِ التَّوْحِيدُ وَأَكْبَرُ مَا نَهَى عَنْهُ الشِّرْكُ.
Walk through the five pillars
The Prophet ﷺ defined Islām as five things. Let's memorize them in Arabic: الشَّهَادَةُ — الصَّلَاةُ — الزَّكَاةُ — الصِّيَامُ — الْحَجُّ. [Repeat 5 times]. Each one has a Qur'ānic dalīl — a proof. The text gives us all of them.
Al-Bayyinah 5 — Ṣalāh and Zakāh
For prayer and zakāh, the text quotes Al-Bayyinah 5: وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ
وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَذَلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ
فَبَدَأَ فِي هَذِهِ الآيَةِ بِالتَّوْحِيدِ وَالْبَرَاءَةِ مِنَ الشِّرْكِ — وَأَمَرَ بِإِقَامَةِ الصَّلَاةِ وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ — وَهَذَا هُوَ مُعْظَمُ الدِّينِ، وَمَا بَعْدَهُ مِنَ الشَّرَائِعِ تَابِعٌ لَهُ — 'They were commanded ONLY to worship Allāh sincerely' — then: وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ. Notice the ORDER in the Qur'ān: Tawḥīd FIRST, then Ṣalāh, then Zakāh. This is the priority order of the entire religion.
Al-Baqarah 183–185 — Fasting
For fasting: Al-Baqarah 183 — يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ — 'O believers, FASTING HAS BEEN WRITTEN upon you.' The word كُتِبَ — 'written' — means required, inscribed. You cannot erase it. And in 185: شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ — Ramaḍān is special because in it Allāh revealed the Qur'ān.
Āl ʿImrān 97 — Ḥajj
For Ḥajj: Āl ʿImrān 97 — وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ — 'And for Allāh upon the people is Ḥajj to the House.' Notice: it says 'upon the PEOPLE' — عَلَى النَّاسِ — meaning all of humanity, not just Muslims. Allāh designed Ḥajj for all, but only the Muslims respond. And the condition: مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ — whoever is ABLE. Allāh is merciful — He only requires what you can do.

Lesson 7 — Ṭahārah, Ṣalāh & Zakāh as ʿIbādah
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Pages 22–24 · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 11B
Lesson 7
Ṭahārah, Ṣalāh & Zakāh — Worship with Body and Wealth الطَّهَارَةُ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالزَّكَاةُ
From the Text — Pages 22–24
Three Types of Worship Mentioned Together وَمِنْهَا: الطَّهَارَةُ وَمِنْهَا: الصَّلَاةُ وَمِنْهَا: الزَّكَاةُ "And from it (worship): Ṭahārah (purification) · and from it: Ṣalāh (prayer) · and from it: Zakāh (charity)"
الطَّهَارَةُ — Purification
إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ التَّوَّابِينَ وَيُحِبُّ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ "Allāh loves those who repent and loves those who keep themselves clean" — Al-Baqarah 2:222
Simple meaning: Wuḍūʾ, ghusl, and staying clean — it is an ACT OF WORSHIP, not just hygiene!
الصَّلَاةُ — Prayer
إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَابًا مَّوْقُوتًا "Prayer has been made required for believers at set times" — An-Nisāʾ 4:103
Simple meaning: 5 prayers a day, at specific times — the most important act of physical worship
الزَّكَاةُ — Compulsory Charity
وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَذَلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ "Establish prayer and give Zakāh — that is the right religion" — Al-Bayyinah 98:5
Simple meaning: Give a share of your money to those in need — because your money is a trust from Allāh
Why Does This Matter?
📖 These are the Qur'ānic proofs the author gives for three major acts of worship

The author includes Ṭahārah (purity), Ṣalāh (prayer), and Zakāh (charity) in the section on types of ʿIbādah — to show that worship is NOT just in your heart. It also means:
  • Washing yourself for prayer = worship
  • Standing up to pray = worship
  • Giving money to the poor = worship
Every act you do FOR ALLĀH becomes worship!
🤔 Think About This

The same actions can be worship OR just ordinary things — depending on your intention (نِيَّةٌ). When you wash your hands before eating — that is normal. When you make wuḍūʾ before prayer — that is WORSHIP. What makes the difference? The intention for Allāh!

🌟
Connecting Everything Together:
Heart worship (fear, hope, trust) + Tongue worship (dhikr, duʿāʾ) + Body worship (prayer, ṭahārah) + Wealth worship (zakāh) = Complete ʿIbādah

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 11B: Ṭahārah, Ṣalāh, Zakāh

  • Know all three types from the text with exact Arabic: وَمِنْهَا: الطَّهَارَةُ / الصَّلَاةُ / الزَّكَاةُ
  • Know the dalīl for Ṭahārah: Al-Baqarah 2:222 — إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ التَّوَّابِينَ وَيُحِبُّ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ
  • Know the dalīl for Ṣalāh: An-Nisāʾ 4:103 — إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَابًا مَّوْقُوتًا
  • Understand that niyvyyah (intention) transforms ordinary acts into worship
  • Connect these three to the comprehensive definition of ʿIbādah from earlier
Connect to earlier lesson
Remember we said ʿIbādah is a big word that covers everything Allāh loves — things you say, do, and feel. We covered the HEART acts. Now the book adds three more: purification, prayer, and charity. These are BODY and WEALTH worship.
Ṭahārah — purity
وَمِنْهَا: الطَّهَارَةُ — From worship: purification. The book gives the ayah: Allāh loves those who repent AND loves those who keep themselves clean. Did you know that making wuḍūʾ is an act of worship? Not just hygiene — WORSHIP. Every time you wash your arms and face for prayer, you're doing something Allāh loves. That's ʿIbādah.
Ṣalāh — prayer
وَمِنْهَا: الصَّلَاةُ — Prayer. The dalīl: إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَابًا مَّوْقُوتًا — "Prayer has been required for believers at SET TIMES." Every prayer has a window of time. Fajr has its time, Dhuhr has its time. You can't move them around to whenever you feel like it. They are fixed acts of worship with fixed times.
Zakāh — charity
وَمِنْهَا: الزَّكَاةُ — Zakāh. Giving from your money to those in need. Now — why is giving money an act of worship? Because your money is a trust from Allāh. It was never really yours. When you give Zakāh you are saying: I know this money belongs to Allāh, and I obey Him in how I use it. That is worship with your wealth.
The intention point
Here is the most important point of this slide: INTENTION. The SAME action can be worship or just a normal thing — depending on why you do it. Washing your hands before dinner — normal. Making wuḍūʾ before prayer — WORSHIP. What changed? The intention. This is why the Prophet ﷺ said: "Actions are judged by their intentions."

Lesson 7 — The Shahādah: Its True Meaning
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 12
Lesson 7 — Islām
What Does Lā ilāha illā Allāh Mean?مَعْنَى لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ
The Greatest Statement — Page 18 لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ مَعْنَاهَا: لَا مَعْبُودَ حَقٌّ إِلَّا اللهُ "Its meaning is: There is no deity TRULY worthy of worship except Allāh."
The Two Parts of the Shahādah
❌ لَا إِلَهَ — The NO part (Nafī)
Rejecting ALL false gods — everything worshipped besides Allāh. Like Ibrāhīm ﷺ said: إِنَّنِي بَرَاءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ — "I am free from what you worship."
✅ إِلَّا اللهُ — The YES part (Ithbāt)
Affirming that Allāh ALONE is truly worthy of worship. Like Ibrāhīm ﷺ said: إِلَّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ — "Except the One who created me — He will guide me."
📝 The word حَقٌّ (ḥaqq) = "truly" is the KEY word. Many things are worshipped — but NONE of them truly DESERVE worship. Only Allāh has the right.
The Qur'ānic Proof — Az-Zukhruf 43:26–28
وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَرَاءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ
إِلَّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ
وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
Sūrat Az-Zukhruf · 43:26–28
Ibrāhīm ﷺ declared: "I am free from what you worship — EXCEPT the One who created me, for He will guide me." And he made it a REMAINING WORD among his descendants — that perhaps they would return.
🌟
وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ
Allāh made لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ a REMAINING WORD among Ibrāhīm's descendants — which includes US. When we say it today, we are continuing the legacy of Ibrāhīm ﷺ!
Youth Educated… Family Cultivated… World Illuminated amanschoolmn.org · amanschool.mn@gmail.com

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 12: Meaning of Lā ilāha illā Allāh — Az-Zukhruf 43:26–28

  • Know the true meaning: لَا مَعْبُودَ حَقٌّ إِلَّا اللهُ — not just 'no god' but 'no TRULY WORTHY deity.'
  • Know the two parts: Nafī (the NO part: لَا إِلَهَ) and Ithbāt (the YES part: إِلَّا اللهُ).
  • Memorize Az-Zukhruf 43:26–28 — Ibrāhīm's declaration.
  • Know the phrase: وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ — and what it means for us.
The critical distinction
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ — the most important words in existence. But what do they MEAN? Most translations say 'There is no god but Allāh.' But that's not precise enough. The scholars say: مَعْنَاهَا: لَا مَعْبُودَ حَقٌّ إِلَّا اللهُ — 'There is no deity TRULY WORTHY of worship except Allāh.' The word حَقٌّ — TRULY — is essential. Why? Because false gods DO exist as things people worship — but they have NO RIGHT to be worshipped.
Nafī and Ithbāt
The Shahādah has two halves. Half one: لَا إِلَهَ — the NO PART. You reject everything false. Like Ibrāhīm ﷺ declared: إِنَّنِي بَرَاءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ — 'I am FREE from what you worship!' Rejection first. Then half two: إِلَّا اللهُ — the YES PART. إِلَّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي — Except the One who CREATED me. You need BOTH halves for a valid Shahādah — rejection + the YES part.
Our inheritance from Ibrāhīm ﷺ
Then Allāh says something beautiful: وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ — 'He made it a REMAINING word among his descendants.' The Shahādah is our inheritance from Ibrāhīm ﷺ — preserved through his descendants until it reaches us TODAY. Every time you say لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ, you're joining a chain of Tawḥīd stretching back thousands of years to the Khalīl of Allāh ﷺ.

Session 5 of 7

Week 5 — Meaning of Shahādah. ~25 min. Al-Zukhruf requires careful explanation.

📋 7-week unit total: 1 session/week × ~60 min = ~7 hours. This slide = ~25 min.

⚠ Do NOT rush. It is better to finish 5 slides deeply than 10 slides superficially.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• The distinction between 'no god exists' (atheism) and 'no TRULY WORTHY deity exists except Allāh' (Tawḥīd) is crucial and often missed. Draw it clearly on the board.

• Nafī and Ithbāt diagram: draw the Shahādah on the board, split it into two halves with a line, label each half (the NO part / the YES part) — students can copy this.

• Az-Zukhruf 43:26–28 is not just poetry — it's the Qur'ānic description of the STRUCTURE of Tawḥīd: first reject false, then affirm the true. This IS the Shahādah template.

• The phrase كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً — a remaining/enduring word — is one of the most beautiful descriptions of the Shahādah. It will remain as long as there are believers. What an honor to carry it.

Lesson 8 — Q6: Our Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله

Lesson 8 — The Prophet ﷺ
Q6: Who is Your Prophet?مَنْ نَبِيُّكَ؟
س ٦وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَكَ: مَنْ نَبِيُّكَ؟ — Who is your Prophet?
Say: Our Prophet is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim ibn ʿAbd Manāf.
فَقُلْ: نَبِيُّنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ بْنِ هَاشِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ مَنَافٍ
Third and final grave question — memorize this answer including the full lineage.
His Selection & Mission — Pages 23–24
Exact Text — Page 23 اصْطَفَاهُ اللهُ تَعَالَى مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ وَهُمْ صَفْوَةُ وَلَدِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَبَعَثَهُ إِلَى الأَحْمَرِ وَالأَسْوَدِ وَأَنزَلَ عَلَيْهِ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ "Allāh chose him from Quraysh — the best of Ismāʿīl's children — sent him to the red and the black — and revealed to him the Book and Wisdom."
الْكِتَابُThe Book
The Qur'ān — the final, preserved revelation of Allāh
الْحِكْمَةُWisdom
The Sunnah — the Prophet's ﷺ teachings, actions, and approval
His Three-Part Mission — Pages 23–24
  • ١
    Called to sincere worship of Allāh فَدَعَا النَّاسَ إِلَى إِخْلَاصِ الْعِبَادَةِ لِلَّهِ
  • ٢
    Called to leave what was worshipped besides Allāh وَتَرْكِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللهِ مِنَ الأَصْنَامِ وَالأَحْجَارِ وَالأَشْجَارِ وَالأَنْبِيَاءِ وَالصَّالِحِينَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ Idols · Stones · Trees · Prophets · Righteous people · Angels — ALL abandoned
  • ٣
    Strove against Shirk until people abandoned it فَدَعَا النَّاسَ إِلَى تَرْكِ الشِّرْكِ وَقَاتَلَهُمْ إِلَى تَرْكِهِ وَأَنْ يُخْلِصُوا لِعِبَادَةِ اللهِ

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 13: Q6 — Who is Your Prophet? + Full Lineage & Selection

  • Memorize Q6 with the full lineage: نَبِيُّنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ بْنِ هَاشِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ مَنَافٍ.
  • Know the exact text: اصْطَفَاهُ اللهُ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ / الأَحْمَرَ وَالأَسْوَدَ / الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ.
  • Know the full list of what Arabs worshipped: أَصْنَام · أَحْجَار · أَشْجَار · أَنْبِيَاء · صَالِحُون · مَلَائِكَة.
  • Know the three-part mission with exact Arabic phrases from the text.
The third grave question
The last of the three grave questions: مَنْ نَبِيُّكَ؟ — Who is your Prophet? And the answer — notice the FULL lineage: نَبِيُّنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ بْنِ هَاشِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ مَنَافٍ. [Drill together]. The lineage is given because knowing WHO your Prophet IS — his complete identity and noble ancestry — is part of truly knowing him ﷺ.
The selection
The text says: اصْطَفَاهُ اللهُ — Allāh CHOSE him. From Quraysh — the most noble Arab tribe. And they are: صَفْوَةُ وَلَدِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ — the best of Ismāʿīl's descendants. Tracing back to Ibrāhīm ﷺ — the Khalīl (Close Friend) of Allāh. And He sent him: إِلَى الأَحْمَرِ وَالأَسْوَدِ — to the red and the black — to ALL of humanity, every color and nation.
What Arabs were worshipping
Now listen to this list the text gives of what Arabs were worshipping BEFORE the Prophet ﷺ came: الأَصْنَامَ — idols. وَالأَحْجَارَ — stones. وَالأَشْجَارَ — trees. وَالأَنْبِيَاءَ — PROPHETS. وَالصَّالِحِينَ — righteous people. وَالْمَلَائِكَةَ — angels. Even prophets and righteous people were being worshipped! This is why the Prophet ﷺ had to CALL people AND FIGHT them until they left all of it and worshipped Allāh alone.
Now drill all THREE grave Q&As
Let's drill all three together now — final practice: مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ [رَبِّيَ اللهُ] · مَا دِينُكَ؟ [دِينِيَ الإِسْلَامُ] · مَنْ نَبِيُّكَ؟ [نَبِيُّنَا مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ]. These are the questions of the grave. Know them with your whole being.

Lesson 8 — The Prophet's ﷺ Life Journey
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 14
Lesson 8 — The Prophet ﷺ
The Prophet's ﷺ Life — Stage by Stageمَرَاحِلُ دَعْوَةِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ
Key Ayah — Al-Anfāl 8:39 (From Page 28) وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّى لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ لِلَّهِ وَالْفِتْنَةُ: الشِّرْكُ "Fight them until there is no more Fitnah — and the religion belongs entirely to Allāh." (Al-Fitnah here = Shirk — as the text explicitly states)
١
Age 40 — Prophethood Begins وَقَدْ بَعَثَهُ اللهُ تَعَالَى عَلَى رَأْسِ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً He called people for approximately 10 years (نَحْوًا مِنْ عَشْرِ سِنِينَ) in Makkah — ONLY to Tawḥīd and leaving Shirk. No prayer, fasting, or Ḥajj required yet. First: foundation.
٢
Al-Miʿrāj — The Night Ascension ثُمَّ عُرِجَ بِهِ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَفُرِضَتْ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَوَاتُ الْخَمْسُ مِنْ غَيْرِ وَاسِطَةٍ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ اللهِ تَعَالَى فِي ذَلِكَ The Five Prayers were required DIRECTLY — with no one in between — between the Prophet ﷺ and Allāh. Every other command came through Jibrīl ﷺ. Ṣalāh was unique.
٣
The Hijrah — Migration to Madīnah ثُمَّ أُمِرَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ بِالْهِجْرَةِ، فَهَاجَرُوا إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ، وَأُمِرَ بِالْجِهَادِ Then Jihād was commanded. He strove approximately 10 more years (نَحْوًا مِنْ عَشْرِ سِنِينَ) until…
٤
People Enter Islām in Multitudes حَتَّى دَخَلَ النَّاسُ فِي دِينِ اللهِ أَفْوَاجًا People entered the religion of Allāh in crowds (أَفْوَاجًا) — the mission that began with one man in Makkah now reached whole tribes and nations at once.
٥
Age 63 — Mission Complete, Passed Away فَلَمَّا تَمَّتْ ثَلَاثٌ وَسِتُّونَ سَنَةً تُوُفِّيَ — وَقَدْ أَكْمَلَ اللهُ تَعَالَى الدِّينَ، وَبَلَّغَ الْبَلَاغَ الْمُبِينَ — صَلَوَاتُ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَامُهُ When 63 years were complete, the Prophet ﷺ passed away. By then Allāh had completed the religion, and the Prophet ﷺ had fully delivered the message entrusted to him.
٦
Mission Summary — Exact Text Page 27 فَضَمَّتْ هَذِهِ الآيَاتُ بَيَانَ مَا بُعِثَ بِهِ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ مِنْ إِخْلَاصِ الْعِبَادَةِ لِلَّهِ، وَالنَّهْيِ عَنْ عِبَادَةِ غَيْرِ اللهِ
قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَدْعُو رَبِّي وَلَا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ أَحَدًا
قُلِ اللَّهَ أَعْبُدُ مُخْلِصًا لَّهُ دِينِي
قُلْ إِنَّمَا أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ وَلَا أُشْرِكَ بِهِ إِلَيْهِ أَدْعُو وَإِلَيْهِ مَآبِ، وَقَصْرِ الْعِبَادَةِ عَلَى اللهِ — وَهَذَا دِينُهُ الَّذِي دَعَا النَّاسَ إِلَيْهِ
"These āyāt contain what the Prophet ﷺ was sent with: sincerity of worship to Allāh, prohibition of worshipping other than Allāh, and restricting worship to Allāh alone."

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 14: The Prophet ﷺ — Life Timeline (Exact Text Pages 28–29)

  • Memorize the key Arabic phrases: وَقَدْ بَعَثَهُ اللهُ عَلَى رَأْسِ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً / نَحْوًا مِنْ عَشْرِ سِنِينَ / دَخَلَ النَّاسُ فِي دِينِ اللهِ أَفْوَاجًا.
  • Know that the Five Prayers were required مِنْ غَيْرِ وَاسِطَةٍ — with no one in between.
  • Know Al-Anfāl 8:39 and that الْفِتْنَةُ here = الشِّرْكُ (as stated in the text).
  • Memorize the mission summary: إِخْلَاصُ الْعِبَادَةِ + النَّهْيُ عَنِ الشِّرْكِ + قَصْرُ الْعِبَادَةِ عَلَى اللهِ.
The profound first 10 years
The text tells us: the Prophet ﷺ was sent at age 40. For the FIRST TEN YEARS — he called ONLY to Tawḥīd. No command for prayer yet. No fasting. No Ḥajj. Just: worship Allāh alone and leave Shirk. Why? Because TAWḤĪD is the foundation. Build the foundation right, then you can add everything else. Ten years for the foundation — that's how important it is.
Ṣalāh's unique honor
Then the Night Ascension. Something extraordinary: وَفُرِضَتْ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَوَاتُ الْخَمْسُ مِنْ غَيْرِ وَاسِطَةٍ — the Five Prayers were required WITHOUT an middleman. Every other command — through Jibrīl ﷺ. But Ṣalāh? Allāh spoke DIRECTLY to His Prophet ﷺ about it. This is why prayer is the pillar of the religion — it's a direct meeting between you and Allāh five times a day.
The conclusion — Exact Text
The text summarizes the Prophet's ﷺ entire mission in one sentence from page 27: إِخْلَاصُ الْعِبَادَةِ لِلَّهِ — sincerity of worship to Allāh. وَالنَّهْيُ عَنْ عِبَادَةِ غَيْرِ اللهِ — prohibition of worshipping other than Allāh. وَقَصْرُ الْعِبَادَةِ عَلَى اللهِ — restricting worship ENTIRELY to Allāh. That's it. That's the whole Prophet ﷺ in three phrases. And he spent 23 years living and teaching this.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• Draw the timeline visually on the board: Age 40 → 10 years Makkah (Tawḥīd only) → Miʿrāj (Ṣalāh required) → Hijrah → 10 years Madīnah (Jihād) → Age 63 (completion).

• The phrase 'with no one in between' (min ghayri wāsiṭa) for Ṣalāh is in the text — it's a famous distinction that sets Ṣalāh above all other obligations. Emphasize it.

• Al-Anfāl 8:39 — the text explicitly defines الفتنة as الشرك. This is important tafsīr. The goal of Jihād was to remove SHIRK from the land, not just political conquest.

• The three-phrase mission summary (إخلاص + نهي + قصر) is a beautiful compression of the entire book. Have students memorize it as the unit summary.

Lesson 9 — Messengers & Companions
Messengers, Companions & the Best Generationsأَوَّلُ الرُّسُلِ وَآخِرُهُمْ وَخَيْرُ الْقُرُونِ
From the Text — Pages 30–31 وَأَوَّلُ الرُّسُلِ نُوحٌ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ وَآخِرُهُمْ مُحَمَّدٌ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَأَفْضَلُ الرُّسُلِ: نَبِيُّنَا ﷺ "The first Messenger is Nūḥ ﷺ · The last is Muḥammad ﷺ · The best of the Messengers is our Prophet ﷺ"
إِنَّا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ كَمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَى نُوحٍ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ مِن بَعْدِهِ
An-Nisāʾ · 4:163 — Proof Nūḥ ﷺ was first
مَّا كَانَ مُحَمَّدٌ أَبَا أَحَدٍ مِّن رِّجَالِكُمْ وَلَٰكِن رَّسُولَ اللَّهِ وَخَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ ۗ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمًا
Al-Aḥzāb · 33:40 — Muḥammad ﷺ is the Seal of Prophets
وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ
"Muḥammad is no more than a Messenger." Āl ʿImrān · 3:144
Best of Humanity After the Prophets — Pages 31–32
  • ١
    Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq أَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ، ثُمَّ عُمَرُ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ، ثُمَّ عُثْمَانُ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ، ثُمَّ عَلِيٌّ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ — وَرَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
  • ٢
    ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ
  • ٣
    ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عَفَّانَ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ
  • ٤
    ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ
Hadīth — The Three Best Generations وَخَيْرُ الْقُرُونِ قَرْنِي ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ ثُمَّ الَّذِينَ يَلُونَهُمْ Al-Bukhārī 2652 · Muslim 6635 "The best of generations is my generation, then those after them, then those after them."
Youth Educated… Family Cultivated… World Illuminated amanschoolmn.org · amanschool.mn@gmail.com

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 15: First Messenger · Last Prophet · Best Companions · Three Generations

  • Memorize: أَوَّلُ الرُّسُلِ نُوحٌ ﷺ · آخِرُهُمْ مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ · أَفْضَلُ الرُّسُلِ نَبِيُّنَا ﷺ.
  • Know An-Nisāʾ 4:163, Al-Aḥzāb 33:40, Āl ʿImrān 3:144.
  • Know the four best companions in order with their Arabic names and رضي الله عنه.
  • Memorize the three-generations hadīth: خَيْرُ الْقُرُونِ قَرْنِي... (Al-Bukhārī 2652, Muslim 6635).
First and Last
The text states: أَوَّلُ الرُّسُلِ نُوحٌ ﷺ — the first MESSENGER is Nūḥ ﷺ. Important distinction: a Nabī (prophet) receives revelation. A Rasūl (messenger) is sent with a law to a people. Ādam ﷺ was a Nabī — Nūḥ was the first Rasūl. And the last: وَآخِرُهُمْ مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ — with the title خَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ from Al-Aḥzāb 40 — Seal of the Prophets. SEALED. Finished. No more.
The Four Caliphs
And after the prophets, the best of humanity: Abū Bakr — then ʿUmar — then ʿUthmān — then ʿAlī — رضي الله عنهم. These are the four Rightly Guided Caliphs. We love them ALL. But we honor them in this specific order — because this is the order of their excellence, as the scholars established.
The three best generations
And the Prophet ﷺ said: خَيْرُ الْقُرُونِ قَرْنِي — 'The best generation is MY generation.' The Ṣaḥābah — the Companions. Then those who come after — the Tābiʿīn. Then those who come after them — the Tābiʿ al-Tābiʿīn. Three generations. This is why in Islām we say: follow the Salaf — the pious predecessors. These three generations are our model.

Session 6 of 7

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• The distinction between Nabī and Rasūl (first Rasūl was Nūḥ ﷺ, first Nabī was Ādam ﷺ) is important ʿaqīdah — mention it clearly.

• Al-Aḥzāb 33:40 — خَاتَمَ النَّبِيِّينَ — Seal of the Prophets — is the definitive Qur'ānic refutation of any claim to prophethood after Muḥammad ﷺ.

• The four Caliphs in order (Abū Bakr → ʿUmar → ʿUthmān → ʿAlī) is the Sunnī ʿaqīdah position on the order of excellence among the Companions.

• The three-generations hadīth is foundational for the Salafī methodology — following the understanding of the early generations in matters of religion.

The Six Pillars of Īmān & the Conclusionأُصُولُ الإِيمَانِ سِتَّةٌ · خَاتِمَةُ الْكِتَابِ
From Text Page 21 — Must Memorize Completely وَأُصُولُ الإِيمَانِ سِتَّةٌ — وَدَلِيلُهُ مَا فِي «الصَّحِيحِ» مِنْ حَدِيثِ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ: أَنْ تُؤْمِنَ بِاللهِ، وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ، وَكُتُبِهِ، وَرُسُلِهِ، وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ، وَبِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ "The foundations of Īmān are six: to believe in Allāh, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and in Al-Qadar — its good and its bad."
Saving Foundations — Page 25 وَمِنْ أُصُولِ الإِيمَانِ الْمُنَجِّي مِنَ الْكُفْرِ: الإِيمَانُ بِالْبَعْثِ، وَالنَّشْرِ، وَالْجَزَاءِ، وَالْحِسَابِ وَالْجَنَّةُ وَالنَّارُ حَقٌّ Resurrection · Spreading Forth · Payback for your deeds · Reckoning · Jannah & Nār are REAL
مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَى
Ṭāhā · 20:55 — Proof of Resurrection
وَإِن تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ أَئِذَا كُنَّا تُرَابًا أَئِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ
وَفِي الآيَةِ دَلِيلٌ عَلَى أَنَّ مَنْ جَحَدَ الْبَعْثَ كَفَرَ كُفْرًا يُوجِبُ الْخُلُودَ فِي النَّارِ وَأُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ
Ar-Raʿd · 13:5 — Denying Resurrection = Kufr
Page 27: Author's Duʿāʾ for Protection
From the Text — Exact Wording Page 27 أَعَاذَنَا اللهُ مِنَ الْكُفْرِ وَأَعْمَالِ الْكُفْرِ "May Allāh protect us from Kufr and the deeds of Kufr."
The Return of ʿĪsā ﷺ — Page 32
وَعِيسَى صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَنزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَيَقْتُلُ الدَّجَّالَ
"ʿĪsā ﷺ will descend from the sky and kill the Dajjāl." — A major sign of the Last Hour. From Muslim 7560.
The Book's Final Words — Page 32 وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ تَمَّتْ عَلَى مَا تَقَدَّمَ "All praise is for Allāh, Lord of all the worlds. Complete — as presented."
🌟 The book opens with الحمد لله رب العالمين and closes with it. What began with praise ends with praise. Everything in between is Tawḥīd.

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 16: Six Pillars of Īmān · Last Day · ʿĪsā ﷺ Returns · Conclusion

  • Memorize the complete Six Pillars: بِاللهِ · وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ · وَكُتُبِهِ · وَرُسُلِهِ · وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ · وَبِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ.
  • Memorize saving foundations: الإِيمَانُ بِالْبَعْثِ وَالنَّشْرِ وَالْجَزَاءِ وَالْحِسَابِ وَالْجَنَّةُ وَالنَّارُ حَقٌّ.
  • Know Ṭāhā 20:55 and Ar-Raʿd 13:5.
  • Know the author's duʿāʾ: أَعَاذَنَا اللهُ مِنَ الْكُفْرِ وَأَعْمَالِ الْكُفْرِ.
  • Know the return of ʿĪsā ﷺ and the closing words: وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ · تَمَّتْ.
The six pillars
The foundations of Īmān — belief — are six: بِاللهِ — in Allāh. وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ — His Angels. وَكُتُبِهِ — His Books. وَرُسُلِهِ — His Messengers. وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ — the Last Day. وَبِالْقَدَرِ خَيْرِهِ وَشَرِّهِ — in Al-Qadar, its good and bad. These are from the Hadīth of Jibrīl in both Al-Bukhārī and Muslim. [Drill together]. Every single one of these is a requirement for valid Īmān.
The saving foundations — Last Day
The text gives us the foundations that SAVE from Kufr — specifically around the Last Day: الإِيمَانُ بِالْبَعْثِ — resurrection. وَالنَّشْرِ — the spreading forth. وَالْجَزَاءِ — payback for your deeds. وَالْحِسَابِ — the reckoning. And: الْجَنَّةُ وَالنَّارُ حَقٌّ — Paradise and the Fire ARE REAL. Not metaphors. Real places that exist now and will be permanent homes based on our choices in this life.
ʿĪsā ﷺ and the Dajjāl
Before closing, the text mentions: وَعِيسَى ﷺ يَنزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَيَقْتُلُ الدَّجَّالَ — ʿĪsā the son of Maryam ﷺ will DESCEND from the sky and kill the Dajjāl. This is a major sign of the Last Hour. ʿĪsā ﷺ never died — he was raised to Allāh. He will return, and when he does, it will be as a Muslim, following the Sharīʿah of Muḥammad ﷺ.
The closing words
And the book ends exactly as it began: وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ — all praise is for Allāh, Lord of all the worlds. تَمَّتْ عَلَى مَا تَقَدَّمَ — complete, as presented. The author began with praise and ended with praise. Because everything — our knowledge, our faith, our Tawḥīd — is a gift from Allāh, and to Him belongs all praise. Let's say it together: الحمد لله رب العالمين.

Session 6 of 7

Week 6 — Six pillars of Īmān, closing. ~15 min. Final new content of the unit.

📋 7-week unit total: 1 session/week × ~60 min = ~7 hours. This slide = ~15 min.

⚠ Do NOT rush. It is better to finish 5 slides deeply than 10 slides superficially.

💡 Tips & Discussion Prompts

• The six pillars should be memorized as a single flowing Arabic sentence — not word by word. Practice choral recitation until it's smooth.

• The duʿāʾ of the author himself — أَعَاذَنَا اللهُ مِنَ الْكُفْرِ وَأَعْمَالِ الْكُفْرِ — is beautiful and should be taught to students as a personal protective duʿāʾ.

• ʿĪsā ﷺ returning as a Muslim following Muḥammad's ﷺ Sharīʿah is important ʿaqīdah that refutes the Christian claim that he will return as a Christian.

• The circular structure of the book (opens and closes with الحمد لله رب العالمين) is aesthetically and theologically beautiful — the author wraps Tawḥīd inside praise of the Lord of the worlds.

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 17: Vocabulary Master Review — All Arabic Terms

  • Know every term in this table with its Arabic spelling and full meaning.
  • Be able to define each term in an age-appropriate sentence.
  • Know which page of the text each term appears on.

Rapid vocabulary review
Let's go through every word we've learned in this unit. I'll say the Arabic — you give me the meaning. Ready? الرَّبُّ [Owner and One Worshipped]. الشِّرْكُ [greatest sin, associating partners]. الدُّعَاءُ [heart and soul of worship]. الطَّاغُوتُ [false god, anything worshipped besides Allāh]. الإِسْلَامُ [surrender, submission, loyalty, rejection]. الإِيمَانُ [faith, six pillars]. الْقَدَرُ [Allāh's plan for everything]. الْبَعْثُ [resurrection]. خَاتَمُ النَّبِيِّينَ [Seal of Prophets — Muḥammad ﷺ].
The three key concepts
The three things that define this entire book: Tawḥīd — know Allāh. ʿIbādah — worship Him alone. Shirk — the thing to never do. Everything else in the religion flows from these three.

Unit Review — The Three Grave Questions
Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd · Shaykh Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb رحمه الله
Slide 18
Unit Review
The Three Questions of the Graveأَسْئِلَةُ الْقَبْرِ الثَّلَاثَةُ
Every Muslim Will Be Asked These Three Questions مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ · مَا دِينُكَ؟ · مَنْ نَبِيُّكَ؟ Who is your Lord? · What is your religion? · Who is your Prophet?
١مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ — Who is your Lord?
رَبِّيَ اللهُ الَّذِي رَبَّانِي وَرَبَّى جَمِيعَ الْعَالَمِينَ بِنِعَمِهِ
"My Lord is Allāh — who nurtured me and all the worlds with His blessings."
٢مَا دِينُكَ؟ — What is your religion?
دِينِيَ الإِسْلَامُ الَّذِي أَسْلَمْتُ لِلَّهِ بِهِ وَآمَنْتُ
"My religion is Islām — through which I surrendered to Allāh and believed."
٣مَنْ نَبِيُّكَ؟ — Who is your Prophet?
نَبِيِّيَ مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَهُ اللهُ رَحْمَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ
"My Prophet is Muḥammad ﷺ — whom Allāh sent as a mercy to all the worlds."
⚡
These questions CANNOT be answered with memorization alone. They require living Tawḥīd — knowing Allāh, worshipping Him alone, and following His Prophet ﷺ — with your heart, not just your tongue.
🤔 Final Reflection

At the beginning of this unit you wrote down "the most important thing a Muslim must know." Open that paper now. Was your answer Tawḥīd? If not — how has this unit changed your thinking?
