📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 18: The Three Grave Questions — Final Drill

  • Answer all three grave questions fluently in Arabic and English.
  • Know that the answers to these questions come from THIS book.
  • Understand that correct answers require living Tawḥīd, not just memorizing words.
  • Reflect on how the unit has deepened understanding of Islām.
Final drill — all three
Stand up. Let's do this standing. I ask — you answer loudly and clearly. مَنْ رَبُّكَ؟ [رَبِّيَ اللهُ!]. مَا دِينُكَ؟ [دِينِيَ الإِسْلَامُ!]. مَنْ نَبِيُّكَ؟ [نَبِيُّنَا مُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ!]. Again — faster. Again — even faster. [Repeat until smooth and confident]. Now sit down.
The deeper point
Here's the thing about these three questions — and this is the most important thing I'll say all unit: the angels won't accept a recited answer. The answers must come from a heart that KNOWS Allāh, SUBMITS to Islām, and LOVES the Prophet ﷺ. If you lived this unit — if you truly understood what we learned — then inshaAllah your heart is ready. If not — keep studying. This knowledge should change how you live.
Return to opening reflection
At the start of this unit I asked you to write down the most important thing a Muslim must know. Take out that paper. Read what you wrote. Has anything changed? [Give students a moment]. Tawḥīd is the answer. And now you know WHY.

📋 Teacher Notes — Slide 20: Closing

  • Close the unit with a duʿāʾ connecting Tawḥīd to eternity — we want to DIE on Tawḥīd, not just learn it.
  • Celebrate student effort and growth throughout the unit.
  • Leave students with a sense of awe and responsibility for the knowledge they carry.
  • Remind students that Tawḥīd is a lifelong practice, not a finished lesson.
Final closing — make it special
الحمد لله. We have completed Taʿlīm al-Ṣibyān al-Tawḥīd — Teaching Children Tawḥīd — by one of the greatest scholars of the last 300 years. And now you are among the students who have studied it. That is a blessing from Allāh. Don't take it lightly.
Final duʿāʾ together
Let us close with a duʿāʾ. Raise your hands. [Lead the duʿāʾ slowly]: اللَّهُمَّ ثَبِّتْنَا عَلَى التَّوْحِيدِ وَتَوَفَّنَا عَلَيْهِ — O Allāh, keep us firm on Tawḥīd and take us in that state. Āmīn. اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنَا مِمَّنْ عَرَفُوكَ فَعَبَدُوكَ — O Allāh, make us from those who know You and worship You. Āmīn. وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ.
Final words
بَارَكَ اللهُ فِيكُمْ. Go carry this Tawḥīd. Live it at home, at school, with your family. That's what the Prophet ﷺ spent 23 years calling people to. And now — it's yours.
⏱ Pacing Guide

Session 7 of 7

Week 7 — Closing, duʼāʼ, and send exam notice home. ~10 min.

📋 7-week unit total: 1 session/week × ~60 min = ~7 hours. This slide = ~10 min.

⚠ Do NOT rush. It is better to finish 5 slides deeply than 10 slides superficially.

💡 Closing Tips

• Give students their certificates or unit completion recognition here if you have them.

• Consider a brief 'Tawḥīd check' oral assessment — call 3-4 students to answer all six Q&As.

• The closing duʿāʾ — اللهم ثبتنا على التوحيد وتوفنا عليه — should become a regular duʿāʾ students say daily.

• Remind students: the test is coming. Use the assignments and test files to prepare them.

✅ MASTERY CHECKLIST — Before Final Exam

Each student must be able to do ALL of these without looking:

📜 Hadith Grading Note (important for older students and parents): The hadith "الدُّعَاءُ مُخُّ الْعِبَادَةِ" (Du'a is the marrow of worship), narrated by Anas and cited in the Sunan — Imam al-Tirmidhi graded it as weak (da'if) in its specific chain. However, the meaning is firmly established by the authentic ayah of Ghafir 40:60 ("Call upon Me, I will answer you") which the book also cites. If an older student asks "is this hadith authentic?" — the honest answer is: the wording is weak in one narration, but the meaning is Quranic. Do not hide this; it teaches students that scholars verify their sources.

  • Recite and explain Q1: Man Rabbuk? + meaning of Rabb + meaning of Allah
  • Recite and explain Q3: Bima ta'rif Rabbak? + name signs + creation + cite Al-A'raf 7:54
  • Recite and explain Q4: Li-ayyi shay'in khalaqak? + cite Al-Dhariyat 51:56
  • Define Ibadah (full definition) + define Shirk (full definition with types)
  • Recite and explain Q5: Ma dinuk? + four meanings of Islam + cite Al Imran 3:19
  • Recite and explain Q6: Man nabiyyuk? + full lineage back to Abd Manaf
  • Name the Five Pillars in order with one proof each
  • Name the Six Pillars of Iman in order
  • Explain Taghut with at least 3 of its types from the book
  • State the first obligation (Kufr bil-Taghut + Iman billah) with its proof

🚨 EMERGENCY — If Something Breaks

  • Blank screen on load: Refresh the page. If still blank, re-download the HTML file.
  • Audio not playing (timer): Known iOS limitation in in-app browsers. Open in Safari directly.
  • Print not working: Open in Safari/Chrome browser, not inside the Claude app preview.
  • Points disappeared: Points save to device storage — only lost if browser data cleared.
  • No projector: Switch to Call & Response and Drill on the teacher phone — no projection needed.
